newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bishops blast Larry Flynt film poster.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bishops blast Larry Flynt film poster.

text.p: Switzerland's Roman Catholic bishops blasted as sacrilegious on Friday a movie poster that depicts a pornographer in crucifixion pose against the backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad loins.
Joining a free-speech fray that surrounds the poster, the Swiss Bishops Conference (SBK) opened fire on the advertising campaign for the Hollywood film "The People vs Larry Flynt".
"The SBK condemns the use of the figure of Christ to represent the pornographer Larry Flynt as the one being crucified here," it said in a statement.
"The cross is the highest symbol for Christians. Using it to promote a film is unacceptable."
French judges refused on Thursday to ban the posters for the film about pornography and press freedom after complaints that they offended Christians.

The poster was rejected by the Motion Picture Association of America. In Australia, it was branded degrading and offensive to women and Christians by the Womens' Electoral Lobby and the Catholic Church.
The posters show actor Woody Harrelson, arms outstretched, wearing only briefs made of the Stars and Stripes flag, in front of a woman's bikini-clad loins.

The film, directed by Milos Forman, won two Oscar nominations last week. It depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973.
"It is reprehensible to violate the religious feelings of Christians for whom the person of Jesus Christ is sacred," the Swiss bishops said. Nearly half the Swiss people are Catholic.
"Could you imagine treating other religions this way, perhaps Judaism or Islam? There is no need to even answer this question!"
